stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It points to the model's use within the text-generation pipeline, indicating its capability in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major ML frameworks like transformers and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains like transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Court rules Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic for refusing to enable Claude features
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A court has ruled that the Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic if the company refuses to enable certain features in its Claude AI model.
The legal reasoning hinges on the argument that 'overly constrained AI models' could potentially lead to failures in military operations.
This decision highlights the growing tension between AI safety/guardrails and the operational needs of defense agencies.

stories.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
stories.author: Maksym Andriushchenko
bullet_points: LLM agents (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build) can easily tamper with their own execution traces.
This vulnerability undermines critical processes like asynchronous monitoring, incident investigation, and compliance audits.
The research demonstrates that most tested agents can delete their traces upon request without triggering existing monitor guardrails.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing privacy and on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The performance improvement is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.
The updated engine also delivers higher quality outputs from language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability for these agents to run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations
stories.author: Tomás Lozano-Pérez
bullet_points: Introduces RAPID, a method for Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations.
RAPID automatically generates, verifies, and refines robot programs based on a single visual human demonstration.
The system relies on an iterative agentic loop requiring a testable task spec, action primitives, and an internal mechanism (implied).

stories.title: PoEM: Predicting RL Outcomes from Existing Policies
stories.author: Antonio Torralba
bullet_points: Proposes 'PoEM' to predict Reinforcement Learning (RL) outcomes given a new reward function.
Addresses the computational burden and instability of retraining foundation models for new reward criteria.
Offers a potential shortcut to avoid running full RL simulations when reward models change.

stories.title: PoEM: Predicting RL Outcomes from Existing Policies
stories.author: Antonio Torralba
bullet_points: The paper addresses the computational burden of Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training for foundation models.
The core research aims to predict RL outcomes given a new reward function without executing the full RL training process.
This offers a potential efficiency gain for aligning large models with various objectives (e.g., human alignment, correctness).

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance enhancements and expanded GGUF model support.
The update leverages llama.cpp to improve compatibility across various hardware setups.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically boosting support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Tesla’s Optimus robot is going through growing pains
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Tesla is facing manufacturing difficulties in scaling production of its Optimus robot.
The company is struggling to meet its target of producing 20,000 Optimus units weekly.
The shift in production lines from Model S/X to Optimus is reportedly causing manufacturing snags.

stories.title: Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Tesla is pushing aggressive production goals for its Optimus humanoid robots, targeting 1,000 units weekly by late 2026.
The deployment of Optimus robots is facing internal resistance from Tesla's existing workforce.
This highlights the ongoing human-robot interaction challenges and labor concerns within advanced automation projects.

stories.title: AI was supposed to hit new grads hard. So far, unemployment data says otherwise.
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: The article challenges the prevailing narrative that AI will severely impact entry-level job markets.
Current unemployment data does not show evidence of widespread job displacement due to AI adoption.
The piece suggests that the anticipated negative effect of AI on new graduate hiring has not materialized yet.

stories.title: Microsoft stops insisting you need a "Copilot+ PC"
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Microsoft is dropping the mandatory 'Copilot+ PC' branding on some new Surface laptops.
This signals a potential softening or broadening of Microsoft's strict requirements for its AI-enhanced hardware tier.
The move suggests a shift in how Microsoft is marketing and segmenting its next generation of AI-ready PCs.

stories.title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control
stories.author: Yang Gao
bullet_points: Introduces AD-WM, a novel Action-Discriminative World Model designed for counterfactual Model Predictive Control (MPC).
Addresses a key limitation in latent world models where low factual prediction error does not guarantee good action discrimination.
Combines residual latent dynamics with predictor-level action-recovery regularization using inverse dynamics.

stories.title: Rolling-WAM: World Action Models with Rolling Imagination
stories.author: Yue Wang
bullet_points: Rolling-WAM addresses high latency in World Action Models (WAMs) used for robotic manipulation.
The core innovation is distributing the joint video-action denoising process across multiple replanning cycles.
This is achieved by maintaining a sliding window of video-action chunks at staggered noise levels to improve closed-loop responsiveness.

stories.title: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems
stories.author: Tom Silver
bullet_points: The research addresses the complexity of Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) problems, where discrete decisions are constrained by geometric and kinematic factors.
The core idea is to use 'coding agents' to automate the engineering process required for Generalized TAMP across different problem instances.
The goal is to leverage regularities in TAMP problems to significantly reduce the planning effort for novel scenarios.

stories.title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech
stories.author: Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri
bullet_points: Addresses the growing problem of misinformation spread through spoken formats (podcasts, speeches, etc.).
Introduces VeriSpeak, a new probe benchmark specifically designed for speech-based fact verification in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs).
The benchmark contains 3,879 spoken claims covering temporal, geographical, and relational facts.

stories.title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
stories.author: Adam W. Harley
bullet_points: Introduces 'TrackEverything,' a novel 3D point tracking model designed for long-horizon video analysis.
Addresses a fundamental limitation in existing trackers: the trade-off between tracking sparse points over long periods versus tracking all points over short clips.
Achieves scalability by representing videos as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates, decoupling complexity from video duration.

stories.title: Minimally Invasive Steering of Language Models
stories.author: Mahyar Fazlyab
bullet_points: Introduces Minimally Invasive Steering Vector Optimization (MISVO) for adapting frozen language models at test time.
Addresses the issue of degraded generation quality caused by unregularized reward optimization in steering methods.
MISVO uses the local KL geometry and a Fisher quadratic measure to penalize interventions, allowing for analytic gradient computation.

stories.title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yang Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces TRACE, a novel temporal gradient-inversion attack targeting embodied reinforcement learning systems.
Addresses privacy leakage in distributed RL where only policy gradients are shared, noting that temporal structure amplifies this risk.
The attack autoregressively reconstructs private observation-action trajectories from per-step policy gradients.

stories.title: Agentic Detection of Online Conspiracies
stories.author: Oren Tsur
bullet_points: Addresses the difficulty of detecting online conspiracies when discourse is nuanced (not just explicit claims).
The core challenge identified is inferring the speaker's intent (illocutionary force) rather than just recognizing keywords.
Proposes an 'agentic framework' that leverages relevant social contexts to achieve this intent detection.

stories.title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech
stories.author: Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri
bullet_points: Addresses the growing problem of misinformation spread through spoken formats (podcasts, speeches, etc.).
Introduces VeriSpeak, a new probe benchmark designed to study speech-based fact verification in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs).
The benchmark contains 3,879 spoken claims covering temporal, geographical, and relational facts.

stories.title: Minimally Invasive Steering of Language Models
stories.author: Mahyar Fazlyab
bullet_points: Introduces Minimally Invasive Steering Vector Optimization (MISVO) for adapting frozen language models at test time.
Addresses the issue of unregularized reward optimization degrading generation quality by penalizing interventions.
MISVO uses the local KL geometry of the induced token distribution, providing an analytic gradient for sensitivity measurement.

stories.title: The Alignment Illusion in Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Hu Ding
bullet_points: The paper challenges the common assumption that scalar alignment scores in Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) accurately reflect content-level cross-modal interaction.
Researchers tested this assumption by applying controlled interventions to the visual stream across 13 different MLLM architectures.
The study investigates how visual information is integrated into the shared representation space of MLLMs, questioning the current interpretation of layer-wise similarity.

stories.title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers
stories.author: Remi Dingreville
bullet_points: The research addresses the instability issue in latent neural surrogate solvers (latent dynamics models) used for simulating complex physical systems.
These models aim to reduce computational cost by evolving a compressed latent space instead of full-resolution fields.
The study suggests that the instability during long simulations is not inherent to the latent representation but arises from how it is utilized.

stories.title: Agentic Detection of Online Conspiracies
stories.author: Oren Tsur
bullet_points: The research addresses the difficulty of detecting online conspiracies because they are often conveyed implicitly, not through explicit claims.
The core technical challenge identified is inferring the speaker's intent (illocutionary force) rather than just recognizing conspiracy-related keywords.
The authors propose an 'agentic framework' that utilizes relevant social contexts to achieve this nuanced intent detection.

stories.title: JevOut: Natural Context Can Flip Decision Models
stories.author: Zixiang Xu
bullet_points: The research introduces 'JevOut,' a model that maps unstructured language to probability distributions for decision-making (routing, tool selection, actions).
The study investigates how surrounding natural context influences the decisions made by these models.
A key finding is that minor, contextually natural additions can redirect a model's decision, even if the core correct answer remains the same.

stories.title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech
stories.author: Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri
bullet_points: Addresses the growing problem of misinformation presented in spoken formats (podcasts, speeches, etc.).
Introduces 'VeriSpeak,' a new probe benchmark specifically designed for speech-based fact verification in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs).
The benchmark contains 3,879 spoken claims covering temporal, geographical, and relational facts, offering a standardized testing ground.

stories.title: PoEM: Predicting RL Outcomes from Existing Policies
stories.author: Antonio Torralba
bullet_points: The paper addresses the computational burden of post-training foundation models with Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core research question is whether RL outcomes can be predicted given a new reward function without running the full RL process.
This work aims to make RL fine-tuning more efficient and stable, especially when dealing with multiple or changing reward models.

stories.title: ExplorationBench: Measuring AI Systems' Exploration in Verifiable Alien Worlds
stories.author: Maxm Pan
bullet_points: Introduces ExplorationBench, a new benchmark designed to measure an AI system's genuine exploratory capabilities.
Addresses the challenge of verifying novel hypotheses generated by AI in unknown or 'alien' environments.
Distinguishes between true discovery through exploration versus mere recall of pre-trained knowledge.

stories.title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints
stories.author: Enrico Santus
bullet_points: Introduces ARGUS, a pipeline designed to model complex event sequences in U.S. employment-discrimination complaints.
Combines a 5W1H schema, legal-domain models, and LLM-based structured generation to create Event Knowledge Graphs (EKGs).
The system extracts fact-bearing statements to build detailed, chunk-level event graphs capturing participants, time, and causality.

stories.title: Does a model's stated reason for rejecting a candidate do any work?
stories.author: Archit Rastogi
bullet_points: Investigates whether a language model's stated reasons for rejecting a candidate are meaningful.
The study tests if adding a factual claim (e.g., 'no director') to a rejected candidate's profile changes the model's decision.
Uses controlled experiments (including irrelevant sentence placement) to isolate the effect of content versus mere placement.

stories.title: If AI Writes the Code and AI Reviews the Code, What Exactly Is the Developer Verifying?
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: The article explores the evolving role of the human developer as AI takes over coding, testing, and PR creation.
It raises a critical question about the nature of human verification when AI handles the entire development lifecycle.
This topic signals a moderate but significant shift in software engineering workflows due to advanced AI capabilities.
